record.paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
record.original_question: For optimal control problems of stochastic distributed parameter systems with endpoint constraints or state constraints, can one derive nontrivial Pontryagin-type maximum principles under genuinely general constraints, for example by extending finite-codimensionality arguments or set-valued-analysis methods to the stochastic setting in a satisfactory way?

evidence.quote: (7) Optimal control problems for SDPSs with endpoint/state constraints. For some special constraints ... one can use the Ekeland variational principle to establish a Pontryagin-type maximum principle with nontrivial Lagrange multipliers. Nevertheless, for the general case, one does need some further conditions to obtain nontrivial results. ... There are some attempts to generalize this condition to the stochastic framework ... Another way is to use some tools from the set-valued analysis ... However, the existing results are still not satisfactory so far.

artifact.category_tag: Stochastic optimal control with state constraints
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an optimal control problem for a stochastic distributed parameter system. Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t\in[0,T]},\mathbb{P})$ be a filtered probability space carrying a cylindrical Wiener process $W$ on a Hilbert space, and let $H$ be a separable Hilbert space. Consider a controlled stochastic evolution equation

$$ dy(t) = \big(Ay(t) + f(t,y(t),u(t))\big)\,dt + g(t,y(t),u(t))\,dW(t), \quad t\in[0,T], \quad y(0)=y_0\in H, $$

where $A$ generates a $C_0$-semigroup on $H$, the control $u(\cdot)$ takes values in a separable metric space $U$ and is $\{\mathcal{F}_t\}$-adapted, and $f,g$ satisfy standard measurability and Lipschitz conditions ensuring well-posedness in a suitable mild-solution sense.

Minimize the cost functional

$$ J(u(\cdot)) = \mathbb{E}\!\left[\int_0^T \ell(t,y(t),u(t))\,dt + h(y(T))\right] $$

subject to either:
(a) an endpoint constraint $\mathbb{E}[\phi(y(T))] \in Q_1$, or pointwise (almost surely) $y(T)\in Q_1\subset H$, where $Q_1$ is a closed convex subset of a Banach space, possibly of infinite codimension; or
(b) a state constraint $y(t)\in Q_2(t)$ for a.e. $t\in[0,T]$, $\mathbb{P}$-a.s., where $\{Q_2(t)\}$ is a family of closed (possibly non-smooth) subsets of $H$.

Problem. Establish a Pontryagin-type maximum principle for optimal pairs $(\bar y(\cdot),\bar u(\cdot))$ of this constrained problem that is nontrivial (i.e., the associated Lagrange multipliers and adjoint processes do not all vanish simultaneously) under genuinely general constraint sets $Q_1$, $Q_2(t)$. In particular, develop a satisfactory extension to the stochastic infinite-dimensional setting of either (i) the finite-codimensionality condition used in deterministic infinite-dimensional control theory, or (ii) set-valued/nonsmooth analytic tools (tangent and normal cones, Clarke generalized gradients, etc.), that yields nontrivial first-order necessary optimality conditions in the form of a stochastic maximum principle, together with the corresponding backward stochastic adjoint equations.
artifact.status_search_result: A search indicates that while Pontryagin-type maximum principles have been established for stochastic distributed parameter systems with special constraints (via Ekeland's variational principle, partial finite-codimensionality extensions, or set-valued analysis), general satisfactory results for arbitrary endpoint or state constraints remain unavailable, and the problem is regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems
status_evidence.snippet: the existing results are still not satisfactory so far
status_evidence.claim: Author surveys list nontrivial maximum principle under general constraints in the stochastic infinite-dimensional setting as still unresolved.
